subject.title: fix: tighten control ui input validation [AI]

question: Should `config.patch` intentionally begin discarding the four legacy accessor-method names even though ordinary property writes do not make them prototype-pollution keys?
rationale: This is a deliberate defense-in-depth versus compatibility tradeoff at a public configuration-write boundary; source inspection can identify the impact, but it cannot establish the repository's intended acceptance policy.

options.title: Preserve accepted names
options.body: Remove the four-name merge-patch rejection and its tests, while retaining the independently proven GitHub preview, avatar, and media filename hardening.

options.title: Approve stricter filtering
options.body: Keep the rejection after a config owner confirms supported config and plugin map paths do not need these identifiers and accepts the silent-drop upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split the policy change
options.body: Land the Control UI and media fixes now and move accessor-name filtering into a focused follow-up with dedicated compatibility discussion.

recommendation.title: Preserve accepted names
recommendation.body: Remove the four-name merge-patch rejection and its tests, while retaining the independently proven GitHub preview, avatar, and media filename hardening.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config migration and compatibility history makes this the best available owner for the accepted-key policy decision.
